_doc: Schema: see docs/reference/api-parity-ledger/SCHEMA.md — the one home for what
a row means. Do NOT copy it back here; issue 1095 is what that cost.

c:context_*.why: rcl splits initialization in two -- an `rcl_context_t` built from a separately-constructed `rcl_init_options_t` -- and threads the context through every entity's init. nano-ros collapses both into `nros_support_t`, which is rclc's `rclc_support_t` name and carries the RMW session INLINE (`_opaque[SESSION_OPAQUE_U64S]`, nros_generated.h:949). The constraint is no allocator: rcl's context hands out a heap `rcl_context_impl_t` and its accessors exist to reach into it, and there is nothing here for them to reach. The useful half lives on `nros_support_*`.

c:get_default_domain_id.why: rcl reads ROS_DOMAIN_ID from the environment at runtime. An embedded backend has no environment (RFC-0036, Domain ID), so the domain arrives through `nros_support_init`'s parameter over a documented ladder -- explicit argument, then hosted env, then the baked default -- with `NROS_DOMAIN_ID_INHERIT`/`NROS_DOMAIN_ID_EXPLICIT_ZERO` sentinels because plain 0 has to stay the UNSET marker (issues 0206/0227).

c:get_zero_initialized_context.why: there is no context type to zero-initialize. `nros_support_get_zero_initialized` is the same idiom on the type we do have.

c:init.why: `rcl_init(argc, argv, options, context)` is the layer BELOW rclc, and rclc's own examples do not call it -- they call `rclc_support_init`, which is what `nros_support_init` mirrors. Declining the lower layer is what makes the C API rclc-shaped rather than rcl-shaped.

c:init_options_*.why: the options half of the same collapse. `rcl_init_options_t` is built, mutated (set_domain_id), copied and finalised before rcl_init consumes it; ours are the two arguments `nros_support_init` takes. There is no `nros_init_options_t`: `nros_support_init(support, locator, domain_id)` takes as arguments the two values rcl's options would carry. CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (phase-417): the sweeping form of this claim -- "there is no runtime options object" -- is false one stage over. Seven ENTITY options structs ship and correlate `same` (see `c:node_options_*`); INIT is a stage that genuinely has none.

c:shutdown.why: as `rcl_init`: the rcl-layer counterpart. `nros_support_fini` is the rclc-shaped teardown.

c:support_get_zero_initialized.why: as `support_is_valid`: rcl's zero-init idiom applied to `nros_support_t`, which rclc does not provide for `rclc_support_t`.

c:support_init_named.why: `nros_support_init` plus a node name. RFC-0046 makes launch the authority on node identity, and an image that was told its name at boot should not have to re-derive it; rclc has no equivalent because a desktop node gets its name from argv.

c:support_init_with_options.why: rclc's options-taking variant. Same constraint as `compile-time-options`: there is no `rcl_init_options_t` to pass.

c:support_is_valid.why: mirrors `rcl_context_is_valid` on the type we actually have. Counted as an extension rather than a rename because rclc -- the C reference -- ships no `rclc_support_is_valid`; we are adding to rclc, not renaming rcl.

c:support_state_t.why: an explicit lifecycle for the support object (uninitialised / initialised / finalised) so a double-init or a use-after-fini is a returned code rather than undefined behaviour. rcl relies on a zero-initialized struct plus `rcl_context_is_valid`; a device that cannot report a crash needs the state to be inspectable.

cpp:Context.why: rclcpp lets several contexts coexist so one process can host independent ROS graphs, and every entity holds a `Context::SharedPtr`. An image is ONE graph and has no allocator for a context registry, so `nros::init()` initialises the single global one and nothing carries a context pointer. The accessors (`get_rcl_context`, `get_sub_context`, `get_init_options`) exist to reach into that per-context state.

cpp:ContextAlreadyInitialized.why: an exception type, and the freestanding builds are -fno-exceptions (RFC-0018). Re-initialising returns `ErrorCode::AlreadyExists` through `nros::Result`.

cpp:InitOptions.why: the C++ face of `rcl_init_options_t`; see `c:init_options_*`. `auto_initialize_logging` and `use_default_domain_id` are runtime toggles for decisions taken at build time here (RFC-0045).

cpp:get_contexts.why: enumerates the process's contexts; there is exactly one and it is not a value you can hold. See `cpp:Context`.

cpp:init.why:
ours is `init(const char* locator, uint8_t domain_id [, const char* node_name])`; rclcpp's is `init(int argc, char** argv, const InitOptions&, SignalHandlerOptions)`. Both take two arguments and share nothing else -- the correlator reports this as `arity-only` for that reason. Three constraints at once: no argv on a device (RFC-0045), no runtime options object, and no POSIX signals. What is left is the two things a device must actually be told, named directly.

phase-428 W6 (2026-09-06) — disposition, required because this row's SHAPE CORRESPONDS: the name exists on the ported surface and the correlator files it `same`, so nothing in a build says the contract differs. That is the class RFC-0089 exists for.

This is the case RFC-0089 Part I is written around, so the disposition is stated against the rule rather than summarised.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclcpp::init(int argc, char** argv, ...)` returns `void` and PARSES `--ros-args` — remaps and parameter overrides reach a process this way.

OURS: `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/nros.hpp:415` — `inline void init(int argc, char const* const* argv)`, which does not parse argv. It scans it with `constexpr detail::argv_has_ros_args` (`:329`) and, if `--ros-args` is present, emits `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_INIT_ARGV` and calls `std::abort()`. The zero-argument `init()` at `:427` is ADOPT outright. The native `nros::init(locator, domain_id)` described above is a different entry point and is unaffected.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: a program with no ROS arguments is unaffected, because nothing was dropped. A program that passes them DIES IMMEDIATELY, naming the flag, instead of running for hours on a remap that was never applied.

WHY THIS IS NOT REFUSE-LOUD AT COMPILE TIME: whether argv carries `--ros-args` is a VALUE, not a type. A `static_assert` on the two-argument overload would reject every caller — including the common embedded one that forwards `main`'s argv and has no ROS arguments at all — and would make upstream's own tutorial `main` unportable. RFC-0089's requirement is LOUDNESS, and compile time is the earliest point loudness is available, not the only point it is permitted. The predicate is `constexpr` precisely so it is separately checkable: its cases are `static_assert`ed in the ordinary compile lane, rather than being observable only by a process that then dies.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06): SITE, re-cited after the header moved -- the scan is `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/nros.hpp:416`, the log is `NROS_ERROR("%s", NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_INIT_ARGV)` at `:420` (message `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/log.hpp:194`) followed by `std::abort()`. Probe: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/ros2_init_argv_refusal.cpp`, which `static_assert`s the predicate's cases including the two mutations that would silence it. The Rust twin is `rust:init_with_args`, now the same shape.

cpp:install_signal_handlers.why: no POSIX signal delivery on Zephyr, FreeRTOS or bare-metal. rclcpp installs a SIGINT handler so Ctrl-C shuts the context down; an image is stopped by its RTOS, a watchdog or a power rail.

cpp:on_shutdown.why: CLOSED as a gap by issue 0790: `nros::on_shutdown(cb, ctx)` now exists, so the names correspond and the row is arity-only rather than theirs-only. What still differs is the SIGNATURE, and the platform constraint is no allocator: rclcpp takes `std::function<void()>`, a heap allocation per callback, while a freestanding no-STL header takes a function pointer plus an opaque `context` and stores the pair in a fixed-capacity static table (`NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS`, default 2). The `out` handle parameter is the third argument for the same reason rclcpp returns one -- so a callback can be removed -- but it is an out-param because this API does not throw and registration can fail with `Full`. The PRE-shutdown phase, which is the half a device actually needs, is `cpp:pre_shutdown` here and `cpp:Executor::add_pre_shutdown_callback` in exec.json.

cpp:pre_shutdown.why: `nros::pre_shutdown(cb, ctx)` -- the free-function spelling of the PRE-shutdown phase over the global executor, next to `nros::on_shutdown`. rclcpp has a free `rclcpp::on_shutdown` but no free pre-shutdown form; having only the post-teardown one as a free function would leave the half that matters on a device reachable only through the executor object. The phase itself is recorded on `cpp:Executor::add_pre_shutdown_callback` (exec.json). Issue 0790.

cpp:remove_on_shutdown_callback.why: Removal counterpart of `cpp:on_shutdown` over the global executor. rclcpp spells it `Context::remove_on_shutdown_callback`; we have no `Context`, so it sits beside the free `on_shutdown` it undoes. Issue 0790.

cpp:remove_pre_shutdown_callback.why: Removal counterpart of `cpp:pre_shutdown` over the global executor. rclcpp's removals live on `Context`, which we do not have; see `cpp:Context`. Issue 0790.

cpp:remove_ros_arguments.why: argv filtering, and there is no argv. RFC-0045 resolves boot config from baked values and the board.

cpp:shutdown.why: phase-428 W6 remainder (2026-09-06) — ledgered because the correlator's return-type comparison became a VERDICT. `rclcpp::shutdown(context, reason)` returns `bool` — `true` when THIS call was the one that shut the context down, `false` when it was already down. Ours (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/node.hpp:181,1031`) returns `Result`. The widening is RFC-0018's and is LOUD for a discarded statement (`Result` is `[[nodiscard]]`), but note what changes for the ported idiom `if (rclcpp::shutdown()) { ... }`: upstream's `false` means "someone else already did it", an ORDINARY answer, while a falsy `Result` means an ERROR. A ported conditional keeps compiling and stops meaning the same thing. Recorded here rather than actioned because the shape is right — an error channel is required — and the fix, if one is wanted, is to make "already shut down" an `ok` rather than a failure. Sibling of `rclcpp::init` returning `void` upstream and `Result` here, which is RFC-0089 Part I's own worked example.

rust:Context.why:
phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `env` joined the measured feature set (`scripts/api_parity/extract_rust.py`, `NROS_FEATURES`), so this type is on the surface for the first time and correlates `same`; it read `theirs-only` before only because the extractor never compiled `src/init.rs`. The old text ("as `cpp:Context` ... neither is available to an image with no env and one session") described the invisible state and is history.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclrs::Context` (0.7.0, `rclrs/src/context.rs`) OWNS the rcl context — built from argv (`Context::new(args, options)`) or the environment (`from_env`, `default_from_env`), it parses `--ros-args`, answers `domain_id()` / `ok()`, and is the factory for executors (`create_executor`).

OURS (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:85`): a plain value `{domain_id, locator, mode, rmw, source}` that the free functions `nros::init()` / `init_with_args` / `init_with_launch*` return, and whose one method `config(node_name)` (`:126`) materialises the `ExecutorConfig` a caller hands to `Executor::open`. It owns nothing and parses nothing: it is the resolved identity, read through the one hosted resolver (`nros::env::try_resolve_hosted`, issue 0687).

Disposition ADOPT-BOUNDED. The name carries the same identity (domain, middleware selection), and `ctx.domain_id` reads where `ctx.domain_id()` did; the envelope is that construction is the free `init*` family (the argv form REFUSES `--ros-args`, see `rust:init_with_args`); `Context::default_from_env()` is the one member that maps 1:1 onto ours, `nros::init()`, and its row is a `rename`, that the executor is opened INTO caller-owned storage from `ctx.config(name)` rather than allocated by the context (RFC-0045; no allocator), and that there is no `ok()` because the value has no shutdown state — liveness is the executor's. Each missing member has its own row below, because the type is `same` and a member gap inside a shipped type is argued on its own (`lookup`'s inheritance rule). The whole module is behind `env`, which requires `std`: an embedded image never compiles it, and its identity arrives through `BootConfig` instead.

rust:Context::new.why:
phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `rclrs::Context::new(args: impl IntoIterator<Item = String>, options: InitOptions) -> Result<Self, RclrsError>`: the argv constructor, which PARSES `--ros-args` (remaps, parameter overrides). Ours is the free function `nros::init_with_args(args)` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:227`), which REFUSES a vector carrying `--ros-args` — see `rust:init_with_args`, the REFUSE-LOUD row — and passes any other vector through to `init()`. A `gap`, not a decline: parsing is owed, and it is remap resolution (RFC-0020 violation class 4), so it lands beside `nros::resolve_name`, and the `InitOptions` half is `rust:InitOptions`. ABSENT as a spelling: `Context::new` is `no function or associated item named new`, which names nothing but is honest; the refusal that names the constraint fires on the free function a porting user is pointed at.

phase-428 closure (2026-09-07) — surveyed for a `rename` with the rest of the `init*` family, and it is NOT one. `Context::new(std::env::args(), InitOptions::new())` maps onto `nros::init_with_args(std::env::args())` only when argv carries no `--ros-args` (otherwise ours refuses at the call, by design) AND the options were default (ours has none) — two facts a reader has to check, not an edit the compiler directs. Stays `gap` + `absent`; the parse is still owed.

rust:Context::from_env.why:
phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `rclrs::Context::from_env(options: InitOptions)`: the environment constructor WITH an options object. The option-less form is `nros::init()` (see `rust:Context::default_from_env`); what this spelling adds is `InitOptions`, whose one field is the domain id, and `rust:InitOptions` records why that arrives through the boot-config ladder (`ROS_DOMAIN_ID` in the env rung, `BootConfig` baked) rather than a mutable options object. Absent: `no function or associated item named from_env`.

phase-428 closure (2026-09-07) — surveyed for a `rename`, and it is NOT one: the argument has no counterpart. `from_env(opts)` maps onto `nros::init()` only when `opts` is `InitOptions::new()` — in which case the caller wanted `default_from_env`, whose row IS the `rename` — and onto nothing when it carries a domain id, which arrives through the boot-config ladder here. Stays `declined` + `absent`.

rust:Context::default_from_env.why:
phase-428 closure (2026-09-07) — RE-VERDICTED gap -> rename. `rclrs::Context::default_from_env() -> Result<Self, RclrsError>`: read the environment, default options. That is EXACTLY `nros::init() -> Result<Context, InitError>` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:177`) under a different spelling — same inputs (`ROS_DOMAIN_ID` and the env rung), same output type, same fallibility, no argument on either side. No platform constraint separates them; the free-function spelling follows rclcpp's `init`, which predates the 2026-09-04 settlement that each language follows ITS OWN upstream (RFC-0089). The mapping is 1:1, so under RFC-0089 the port is MECHANICAL: rustc says `no function or associated item named default_from_env found for struct Context`, and the edit is the one line in `rename.resolution`.

The Q1 follow-through row filed this `gap` + `absent` on the grounds that the entry-point spelling is one decision for the four `init*` functions. The closure survey (phase-428 doc, closure §2) found that only THIS member maps 1:1: `Context::new` takes argv it PARSES and an options object (ours refuses the flag and has no options), `Context::from_env` takes the options object, and the two launch forms have no upstream candidate at all. So the decision is about one alias, not a family, and `rename` is the honest verdict — the capability is present under another spelling, which `gap` ("nobody has done it") did not say. Disposition stays `absent`: today the name does not exist and the compiler says so, which is the loud half of the bargain; this row is what to type. The ours-only half is `rust:init`.

rename.resolution: PORT, mechanical: `let ctx = Context::default_from_env()?;` -> `let ctx = nros::init()?;`. Same `Result`, same `?`; the error type differs (`InitError`, see `rust:RclrsError`), which matters only where the caller's own signature names `RclrsError`. What the caller does NEXT is the row above (`rust:Context`): `Executor::open(&ctx.config(name))` instead of `ctx.create_executor(..)`.
rename.blocker: Whether to ADD the rclrs spelling beside ours, not whether ours goes: `impl Context { pub fn default_from_env() -> Result<Context, InitError> { init() } }` in `init.rs` behind `env`, two lines, and the port stops needing this row. `init()` stays either way — it anchors `init_with_args` and the launch-aware forms. RFC-0089 clause 2 permits it and nothing forbids it; the cost is a second spelling of one function on the Rust surface, and phase-428's scope note says this sweep does not rename. Maintainer's call, named in the closure report.

rust:Context::domain_id.why: phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `rclrs::Context::domain_id(&self) -> usize`, an accessor over the rcl handle. Ours is the public FIELD `Context::domain_id: u32` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:87`): the value is a plain struct with nothing to hide, so the field is the accessor. A ported `ctx.domain_id()` fails to compile — rustc says the name is a field, not a method, and offers to remove the parentheses — so the difference is loud and self-correcting, but it is a per-call-site edit paid for by no constraint, which is what makes it a gap rather than a divergence. One `pub fn domain_id(&self) -> u32` closes it.

rust:Context::ok.why: phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `rclrs::Context::ok(&self) -> bool`: whether the rcl context is still valid, i.e. `shutdown` has not been called on it. Our `Context` is a resolved VALUE (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:85`) with no shutdown state to report; the thing that can stop being live is the session, and that is the executor's (`Executor::open` / its spin verbs return the failure, `rust:Executor::spin`). A method that always answered `true` would be the silent-disagreement RFC-0089 forbids, so there is none. Absent: `no method named ok`.

rust:Context::config.why: phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `Context::config(&self, node_name) -> ExecutorConfig` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:126`): the one method on our `Context`, turning the resolved identity into the config `Executor::open` takes, with the node name supplied at the call because one process can open several nodes on one identity. rclrs has no counterpart: its `Context` is passed to `create_node` / `create_executor` directly, because it owns the rcl context those consume. Ours owns nothing (see `rust:Context`), so the seam between identity and session is an explicit conversion. Borrowing (`ExecutorConfig<'a>` over `&'a self`) is what keeps the config heap-free.

rust:ContextSource.why: phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `enum ContextSource { Env, Launch }` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:105`), the `source` field on `Context`: which `init*` entry point produced it, for diagnostics and tests. No upstream counterpart — rclrs has one constructor family. One caveat the row must carry because the enum's own doc does: `Launch` means the launch-aware entry point was CALLED, not that a launch file was parsed — `init_with_launch` checks the path exists and reads the launcher's projected environment (`rust:init_with_launch` records that finding), so introspection on this value confirms more than happened.

rust:InitError.why: phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — the error type of the hosted init surface (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:47`): `LaunchFileNotFound`, `LaunchParseFailed` (declared, unused until the launch XML is parsed in-process — see `rust:init_with_launch`), `EnvParseFailed`. rclrs folds the same failures into `RclrsError`, whose row (`rust:RclrsError`) records why a source-chained, message-carrying error is not available here; this one is flat and `Copy`-free on purpose. Implements `core::error::Error`. Visible since `env` joined the measured feature set.

rust:REFUSE_INIT_ARGS.why: phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — the text `init_with_args` refuses with (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:185`): the `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_INIT_ARGV` message with the Rust spellings, public so a wrapper or a test can match on it rather than on a substring that drifts. rclrs has nothing to refuse — it parses the arguments. See `rust:init_with_args`, the row the refusal belongs to.

rust:args_have_ros_args.why: phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — the refusal's predicate, separately callable (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:202`): exact match on `--ros-args` over any `AsRef<str>` iterator. Public for the reason RFC-0089 §"where the refusal fires" gives — an abort inlined into `init` can only be observed by a process that then dies — so the unit test that pins the mutation (`--ros-args-extra` is NOT the flag) runs on a function, not a process. No upstream counterpart; rclrs's argument scan is internal to `Context::new`.

rust:InitOptions.why: as `cpp:InitOptions`; the domain arrives through the boot-config ladder, not a mutable options object.

c:support_init_rmw.why: `nros_support_init_named` plus a backend selector -- it names the RMW backend the session opens against. rclc/rclcpp have no counterpart because a ROS 2 desktop process selects its middleware with the `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION` environment variable, and an embedded image has no environment to read -- which is precisely how issue 1050 happened: the selector had an env rung and no baked one, so a PX4 module declaring `BACKENDS uorb` could not say so and the registry's first entry won. The hosted env rung (`$NROS_RMW`) still takes precedence, matching `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION`'s authority; this is the rung beneath it.

rust:init.why:
phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — REWRITTEN. This row's text was about `nros::logging::init` (the `nros-log` emission surface phase-417 W4.d re-exported through the facade); that text now lives where it belongs, and the mis-filing is what the orphan-refs gate's docstring records.

`nros::init() -> Result<Context, InitError>` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:177`, behind feature `env`): read `ROS_DOMAIN_ID`, `NROS_LOCATOR`, `NROS_SESSION_MODE` and `NROS_RMW` / `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION` through the one hosted resolver (`nros::env::try_resolve_hosted`, issue 0687 — this function used to carry its own copy of the parse and the copies had drifted) and return the resolved identity as a `Context` tagged `ContextSource::Env`. The caller opens the session itself: `Executor::open(&ctx.config(name))` then `spin_blocking` or a `spin_once` loop. It does not install signal handlers (`cpp:install_signal_handlers` records why, and the Rust surface has none either) and it does not read argv (`rust:init_with_args` is the argv form and REFUSES `--ros-args`).

rclrs has no free `init`: its equivalent is `Context::default_from_env()`, 1:1 in inputs, output and fallibility, and `rust:Context::default_from_env` is the theirs-only half of this pair.

phase-428 closure (2026-09-07) — RE-VERDICTED extension -> rename. `extension` says ROS 2 has none, and rclrs has this one under another name; the two halves are one statement seen from two sides (SCHEMA.md's rule for a pair). What kept it `extension` was that the free function also anchors `init_with_args` and the launch-aware forms, which rclrs does not have — true, and not a reason: those three keep their own rows (`refuse-loud`, and two `extension`s with no upstream candidate), and nothing about them moves if `Context::default_from_env()` is added beside `init()`. The verdict records that OURS is the spelling that differs; whether it gains the rclrs spelling (an alias, never a removal) is `rename.blocker`, and the port a user makes today is written on the other half.

rename.resolution: Pair of `rust:Context::default_from_env`, where the porting edit is written. `init()` is not removed under any outcome; the open question is only whether the rclrs spelling is added beside it.

rust:init_with_args.why:
phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-11, first of three. The Rust twin of the `rclcpp::init(argc, argv)` case RFC-0089's Part I is written around.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: rclrs takes the process arguments through `Context::new(std::env::args())` and PARSES them — `--ros-args`, remaps, parameter overrides. Passing argv is how a node gets its runtime identity.

OURS (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:186`): `pub fn init_with_args<I, S>(_args: I)`. The parameter is named `_args`; the body is `init()`; the doc says it is "a thin wrapper over `init` that ignores the args" and carries a TODO to parse them.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: SILENTLY WRONG. `init_with_args(std::env::args())` compiles and returns `Ok`; `--ros-args -p foo:=42` is discarded and the node runs on defaults for as long as it runs.

DISPOSITION REFUSE-LOUD, and it follows the decision already taken for the C++ sibling rather than inventing one: RFC-0089 §"where the refusal fires" settles that `init(argc, argv)` may compile, must scan for `--ros-args`, and must abort naming the flag when it is present — because only the VALUE carries the defect, so the earliest point it is KNOWABLE is the call. Argument PARSING itself is remap resolution, RFC-0020 violation class 4, so it belongs beside `nros::resolve_name` and not in a wrapper — which is why the refusal, not the parser, is the item that can land first. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) — the refusal is IMPLEMENTED; this row now describes shipped code, and the paragraph above ("OURS ... ignores the args") is history. `packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:227` — `init_with_args` scans the iterator with `args_have_ros_args` (`:202`, exact match on `--ros-args`, separately unit-tested so a prefix match on `--ros-args-extra` cannot creep in) and, when the flag is present, logs `REFUSE_INIT_ARGS` (`:185`, the `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_INIT_ARGV` text with the Rust spellings) through `nros_log` and panics with the same text. A vector with no ROS arguments passes through to `init()` unchanged. Tests: `init::ros_args_refusal_tests` (`cargo test -p nros --features env,std`) — two `#[should_panic(expected = "--ros-args")]` cases, one pass-through, and the predicate's mutation control.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT, now: the process dies at `init_with_args` naming the flag and the alternative, the shape `rclcpp::init(argc, argv)` has in `nros.hpp:416`. The verdict stays `gap`: parsing `--ros-args` is still owed, and it belongs beside `nros::resolve_name` (RFC-0020 class 4), not here.

rust:init_with_launch.why:
phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-11, second of three. NO DISPOSITION IS WRITTEN. The four dispositions are what clause 1 does to a CANDIDATE FROM CLAUSE 2 (RFC-0089); this item has no upstream candidate, so there is nothing for a constraint to permit, weaken or refuse. — rclrs has no launch-model entry point; the C++ twins are `cpp:init_with_launch` / `cpp:init_with_launch_auto` in the node stage, and this row is their missing Rust counterpart as well as the finding.

THE FINDING: `packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:228` checks that the path EXISTS (`if !p.exists() { return Err(InitError::LaunchFileNotFound) }`) and then calls `read_env_context(ContextSource::Launch)`. It never parses the file. The returned `Context` reports `source == Launch`, so introspection CONFIRMS that the launch file was honoured when only its existence was.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: SILENTLY WRONG, and the diagnostic actively misleads — a well-formed launch file with the wrong contents and an empty file that happens to exist produce identical, successful results. RFC-0046 makes launch authoritative for node identity, which is precisely why an unparsed one must not report `Launch`. The honest intermediate state is to report the source we actually used, or to refuse at the call naming the unparsed file. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:212` is `read_env_context(ContextSource::Launch)` with NO path resolution at all — the three-step bringup resolution its own doc describes is marked "(NOT yet consumed; placeholder)". It returns a `Context` whose source says `Launch`. SILENTLY WRONG, for the same reason and with the same remedy as `rust:init_with_launch`; see that row. Both are `#[cfg(feature = "env")]`.
